title: Coldstart
tagline: A job-search pipeline that does the legwork.
description: Changed-feed ingestion, resume-aware LLM scoring, and an auditable daily digest. Built to run unattended.
problem: Job feeds contain far more postings than one person can use. Freshness, location, eligibility, and fit all matter, but evaluating every raw record with an LLM is slow and expensive.
approach: Poll the upstream manifest and download changed ATS slices. Apply deterministic title, company, freshness, location, and eligibility filters before scoring.
Route surviving jobs to one of four resume tracks. Score with a configured hosted model or local Ollama, and retain outcomes and failure details in SQLite.
Export a CSV audit trail and send a scheduled digest. Persist the email-send guard so restarting the daemon does not repeat the day’s digest.
outcome: A complete local workflow from public ATS data to a ranked review surface, with explicit spending limits, retry behavior, and an audit trail.
tradeoff: Deterministic filters do the inexpensive work first. Model scoring is reserved for postings that survive those gates; uncertain location data is retained rather than silently discarded.

title: Role Collector
tagline: Find the opening before it gets buried.
description: An autonomous discovery agent spanning ATS APIs, search, and company watchlists, with freshness-first review.
problem: A useful job-sourcing system needs more than a list of career pages. It must discover openings across sources, extract inconsistent pages, recognize duplicates, and preserve when a posting was actually observed.
approach: Combine ATS API discovery, targeted search, funding events, company watchlists, and public LinkedIn posts in a node-based workflow.
Extract through an ATS parser, JSON-LD, DOM parsing, and optional LLM fallback. Normalize timestamps and keep source metadata alongside each job.
Check exact idempotency and semantic similarity before persistence. Surface results in a FastAPI/Jinja2 dashboard with freshness buckets and filters.
outcome: An end-to-end discovery, extraction, storage, and review workflow across six ATS connectors, with configurable Langfuse tracing.
tradeoff: Freshness is explicit data, not a guess based on sort order. Source timestamps and first-observed timestamps remain separate, including an unknown bucket when neither supports a confident claim.

title: SimCricketX
tagline: A cricket match, modeled ball by ball.
description: A probabilistic simulation engine with live match state, built and operated as a complete solo project.
problem: A cricket simulation needs plausible outcomes and consistent match state. Concurrent requests must not apply the same delivery twice or leave different clients looking at different games.
approach: Model ball outcomes using match phase, momentum, and pressure. Send live state changes over WebSockets.
Build a modular Flask REST API backed by a 13-model SQLAlchemy schema with indexed queries and cascade deletes.
Use per-match threading locks and a single-worker, multi-thread Gunicorn deployment to keep in-memory state coherent. Operate it on OCI behind Nginx.
outcome: Served 13,000 active users and resolved a 120-delivery match in under five seconds.
tradeoff: A single worker simplifies shared match-state correctness. Per-match locks protect updates, at the cost of limiting scale to that process until state is moved behind a shared coordination layer.

title: Async Audio Pipeline
description: Independent transcription and summarization workers behind a lightweight FastAPI job interface.
problem: Processing a long recording inside an API request ties the caller to the slowest stage. Splitting, transcription, and summarization have different compute needs and failure modes.
approach: Let FastAPI accept a job, return its ID, and report progress. Keep queues, job state, and results in Redis.
Separate the Splitter, Transcriber, and Summarizer into independent workers using Whisper and Gemini.
Use idempotent retries so a failed task can be retried without requiring the client to restart the whole workflow.
outcome: Reduced turnaround for a one-hour meeting from 45–75 minutes to 7–11 minutes.
tradeoff: The API remains responsive while worker capacity can scale independently. The queue and job-state model become critical infrastructure and must preserve retry semantics.

title: JobPulse
tagline: One place for the whole job search.
description: A self-hosted dashboard for fresh jobs, application tracking, company blocklists, and search analytics.
problem: Finding openings and keeping track of applications often happen in disconnected tools. A small self-hosted application can unify those workflows without needing a large infrastructure footprint.
approach: Build on the vendored jobhive / ats-scrapers library, scheduling ingestion and normalizing results into a local SQLite database.
Use WAL mode, FTS5 full-text search, and synchronization triggers. Preserve application history separately from the expiring job feed.
Serve JSON endpoints and an interactive FastAPI, Jinja2, and HTMX interface for browsing, applying, filtering, and reviewing scrape logs.
outcome: A cohesive self-hosted workflow for job discovery and application tracking, with per-run audit records and a searchable feed.
tradeoff: SQLite and server-rendered interactions keep the application small. The project builds on an existing scraper library rather than claiming every connector as original work.

title: Resume Tailor AI
tagline: From the job page to a tailored resume.
description: A Chrome extension and FastAPI service that turn job context into tailored PDF and DOCX documents.
problem: Tailoring a resume usually means moving between the job description, a document editor, and export tools. The extension keeps the entry point on the job page.
approach: Capture job descriptions through a Manifest V3 Chrome extension and send structured resume profiles to a FastAPI backend.
Use Google Gemini to extract keywords and suggest tailored resume content. Return matched and missing keywords with a heuristic compatibility score.
Render PDF documents from Jinja2 templates through WeasyPrint, and editable Word documents through python-docx.
outcome: An integrated capture, tailoring, and document-generation workflow with reviewable AI output.
tradeoff: The compatibility score is keyword feedback, not a guarantee of passing an employer’s ATS. AI suggestions still need factual review before sending a resume.

title: CodeMate
description: A Gemma and QLoRA experiment, from instruction-dataset preparation to saved adapter artifacts.
problem: Adapting a general language model to coding tasks needs a reproducible path from instruction examples to training artifacts. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning makes that workflow more approachable.
approach: Convert CodeAlpaca-20k instruction, input, and response examples into consistent JSONL training records.
Load Gemma in 4-bit precision and configure PEFT LoRA adapters on query and value projections.
Use gradient accumulation during training and save the model and tokenizer artifacts for subsequent inference experiments.
outcome: A reproducible workflow for parameter-efficient Gemma fine-tuning on code instruction data.
tradeoff: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning reduces training memory requirements while keeping the base model frozen. Training data quality and evaluation remain essential to useful coding assistance.

title: AI-Driven Resume Builder
tagline: Structured content in. Application-ready files out.
description: A Python CLI that combines YAML resume data, LLM tailoring, and LaTeX document generation.
problem: A resume is easier to reuse when its content is structured separately from its layout. The challenge is carrying that structure through job-specific tailoring and repeatable document output.
approach: Validate YAML resume data and normalize it into JSON before passing it through the rest of the pipeline.
Use the job description and Perplexity API to tailor the structured content.
Fill a LaTeX template, orchestrate PDF/DOCX conversion, and collect the generated artifacts into a named output directory.
outcome: A command-line workflow that separates resume content, tailoring, and document formatting into explicit stages.
tradeoff: LaTeX gives strong layout control but brings platform-specific tooling. The repository documents Windows/MikTeX PDF generation and manual compilation on macOS.

title: Emotion Detector
description: A text-classification application comparing classical ML and neural predictions across six emotions.
problem: Text emotion classification is a useful way to compare modeling choices on the same input. A small application makes the differences between model predictions inspectable.
approach: Normalize input with NLTK tokenization, stop-word removal, and lemmatization, then transform it into TF-IDF features.
Run Logistic Regression, SVM, and a Keras MLP to classify sadness, joy, love, anger, fear, or surprise.
Expose predictions through a Flask web interface and a JSON prediction API.
outcome: An interactive model-comparison interface backed by saved vectorizer and model artifacts.
tradeoff: The three model outputs are comparisons, not calibrated confidence estimates. This case study avoids repeating evaluation scores that were not independently reproduced.

title: Piko contribution
tagline: A small change, through the whole review path.
description: Extending recommended flags from booleans to long-typed MobileConfig overrides in an existing codebase.
problem: Piko’s recommended-flags mechanism handled boolean values. Supporting long-valued MobileConfig flags required a change that fit the project’s existing bytecode patching approach.
approach: Extend the recommended-flags system to carry long-typed overrides.
Hook long-returning accessors in bytecode, preserving the surrounding patching flow.
Carry the contribution through maintainer review in the upstream project.
outcome: An upstream contribution recorded in PR #1741, with the implementation and review available in the public repository.
tradeoff: Contributing within an established project means respecting its abstractions and maintenance constraints, not just making a local change work.
